points.description: Reusability: states that code/classes can be reused (e.g. through inheritance, libraries, or creating many objects from one class), reducing duplication and development effort. Equivalent wording accepted (e.g. 'code reuse', 'inheritance allows reuse').

levels.says: Mentions reusability or inheritance only by name, without saying what is reused or why it helps.

points.description: Abstraction: states that complexity/implementation details are hidden and only essential features are exposed (via classes, objects, interfaces). Naming 'abstraction' with a basic correct meaning earns full marks.

levels.says: Names abstraction only, with no or incorrect explanation of what it means.

points.description: Encapsulation / data security: data and methods are bundled in objects and access is controlled (private data, data hiding), protecting data from unintended modification.
Modularity / maintainability: program is divided into self-contained objects/classes, making code easier to understand, modify, debug, test and maintain.

Any other valid advantage, e.g. polymorphism/flexibility and extensibility, scalability for large programs, or modelling real-world entities naturally. Must be a distinct idea from P1–P4; at most one credited.

rubric.notes: The model answer (abstraction and reusability) should earn at least 3 of 5 here, with credit for explaining each. Award marks for each distinct valid advantage, with explanation earning more than a bare name. Do not give credit twice for the same idea, and no marks for disadvantages or non-OOP features (e.g. speed).
rubric.answer_key: Main advantages of OOP: reusability (inheritance, classes reused, less duplication); abstraction (hiding complexity, exposing essentials); encapsulation/data security (data hiding); modularity and easier maintenance/debugging; polymorphism and extensibility/flexibility; models real-world entities and scales to large programs.

selftest_notes: The model answer scored only 1.8 of 5.
